thread.title: Alphabet, Apple Weigh On Market As Rate Hike Views Sink Stocks

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Alphabet, Apple Weigh On Market As Rate Hike Views Sink Stocks
text:
Key market indexes were down hard Tuesday as Alphabet ( GOOGL ) weighed on techs and the 10-year Treasury yield hit 3% for the first time since 2014, raising expectations for four Fed rate hikes this year.
X SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) slumped 2%, PowerShares QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) also tumbled 2% and SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ) sank 1.4% in the stock market today . Foreign markets held up better as iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ( EEM ) and iShares MSCI EAFE ( EFA ) gave up 0.3% each.
3M ( MMM ), which reported quarterly earnings in line with views, weighed on the Dow with an 8.5% drop. Caterpillar ( CAT ) reversed to a 6% loss, while Boeing ( BA ), Travelers ( TRV ) and DowDuPont ( DWDP ) each fell 4% or more.
Apple ( AAPL ) shed 1.4% as it slid further below its 200-day moving average and extended its losing streak to five. Shares have fallen amid reports of weaker iPhone demand. Related chip stocks took another hit Tuesday as analysts cut their ratings and/or price targets on iPhone chip suppliers. VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ( SMH ) fell 0.9%.
Among other techs, Alphabet lost 4.5% to test its 200-day moving average. The Google parent late Monday reported Q1 results that beat views on both the top and bottom lines, but its traffic acquisition costs were higher than expected. The rest of the FANG stocks also fell: Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ) and Netflix ( NFLX ) were down about 4% apiece.
The biggest sector fund decliners included industrials, biotech and technology ETFs. Gold miners, utilities and real estate led the upside among sector plays. Gold futures climbed 0.5% to $1,330.40 an ounce.
Bitcoin gained 5% to $9,408.25, according to CoinDesk . Bitcoin Investment Trust ( GBTC ) popped 9% as it pads gains above its 50-day line and extends its win streak to five.
Surging Oil New sector leaders are emerging in the exchange traded fund universe as oil prices surge to three-year highs amid continued unrest in the Mideast.
Energy is ranked No. 10 among the 33 sectors tracked by IBD . Dig a bit deeper into the sector and you'll find most oil & gas industry groups have moved up the ranks from three weeks ago: U.S. exploration & production to No. 16, up from No. 59, oilfield services to No. 21 from No. 94, oil machinery to No. 24 vs. No. 79.
Other risers in the top 50 industry groups include: Refining to No. 33 vs. No. 93, drilling to No. 35 vs. No. 110, and international exploration & production, No. 38 vs. No. 139.
So it shouldn't be too surprising to see several oil-and-gas ETFs building bases or getting close to potential buy points . SPDR S&P Oil & Gas Exploration & Production ( XOP ) continues to work on the right side of a three-month cup base with a 40.29 entry.

Please contact customer service CLOSE The $2.5 billion fund, which tracks the S&P Oil & Gas Exploration & Production Select Industry Index, will mark its 12th anniversary in June. E&P stocks made up just north of 78% of assets, refining & marketing about 16%, and integrated oil & gas the remaining 5.5%. Top holdings as of April 20 included QEP Resources ( QEP ), Whiting Petroleum ( WLL ), Carrizo Oil & Gas ( CRZO ) and HollyFrontier ( HFC ).
XOP's 4.7% year-to-date gain through Friday, according to Morningstar Direct, outpaces the S&P 500's 0.4% return. But the ETF sharply lags the S&P 500 based on its average annual performance over the longer haul, with losses over the past three, five and 10 years vs. the broader index's 10.6%, 13.8% and 9.1% gains for those respective periods. It carries a 0.35% expense ratio.
Jeffrey Gundlach, chief investment officer of investment manager DoubleLine Capital, recommended going long in XOP and shorting Facebook ( FB ) at a conference in New York. He favors commodities, which tend to outperform in the latter stages of the economic cycle.
West Texas intermediate crude oil prices rose 1% Monday to $68.95 a barrel.
